तक्षक: Takṣaka m.: A mythical serpent. A. Birth and family: One of the sons (very likely the fourth son) of Kadrū (and Kaśyapa), hence called काद्रवेय 1. 31. 5, 2; 1. 59. 40 (placed third); 1. 3. 144; his youngest brother (जघन्यज) was Śrutasena 1. 3. 146; his son Aśvasena (1. 218. 5) was his constant companion 1. 3. 145; (by तक्षक-पुत्र 8. 65. 39 Aśvasena is probably alluded to); his daughter Jvālā married to Ṛkṣa born in the line of Pūru 1. 90. 24; serpents belong-ing to his कुल, Pucchaṇḍaka and others, listed by Sūta among those offered in the snake sacrifice of Janamejaya 1. 52. 7-9; Takṣaka also named among the serpent-sons of Surasā and Kaśyapa 5. 101. 9, 4, 17. B. Residence: Lived in Bhogavatī Purī in the southern direc-tion; he, with Vāsuki, protected it 5. 107. 19; 5. 101. 9; he had his abode (निवेशन) also in the Khāṇḍava forest where Asura Maya happ-ened to stay at the time of the great fire 1. 215. 7; 1. 219. 35; Uttaṅka, in his praise of the नागस्, referred to Takṣaka as living in Khāṇḍava near Kurukṣetra, along the river Ikṣumatī 1. 3. 142-146. C. Status: Second only to Vāsuki according to an enumeration based on eminence (यथाश्रेष्ठान्) 5. 101. 8; called the king of the serpents नागराज 1. 3. 119, 120, 166; सर्पराज 1. 218. 4; chief of serpents नागेन्द्र 1. 38. 34; 1. 39. 3; पन्न-गेन्द्र 1. 38. 33, 35 etc.; best among ser-pents पन्नगोत्तम 1. 37. 13, 19, etc.; भु-जगोत्तम 1. 48. 15, 18; पन्नगश्रेष्ठ 1. 38. 32, 36; 1. 40. 3; उरगसत्तम 1. 39. 16; however Uttaṅka called Takṣaka पन्नगा-धम 1. 3. 188. D. Description: He was of blazing lustre (तिग्मतेजस्), his poison acted like fire and burnt the being he bit (आशीविष) 1. 37. 13; lotus-coloured (पद्म-वर्चस्) 1. 40. 3; he was called by Uttaṅka and Janamejaya ‘evil-minded’ (दुरात्मन् 1. 46. 36, 40; दुष्टान्तरात्मन् 1. 3. 185, 187), and by Janamejaya ‘sinful’ (पाप) 1. 46. 37. E. Khāṇḍava incident: Since Takṣaka lived in the Khāṇḍava forest, whenever god Fire tried to burn it, Indra, being Takṣaka's friend, he immediately extinguished the fire 1. 215. 7; when the forest was finally on fire, Takṣaka was not in Khāṇḍava but was safe at Kurukṣetra 1. 218. 4; Indra was informed of this by an invisible voice 1. 219. 12-13. F. Takṣaka and the कुण्डलस्: Uttaṅka informed by Pauṣyaś wife (क्षत्रिया) while handing over her ear-rings to him that Takṣaka coveted them; Uttaṅka assured her that Takṣaka would not be able to attack him 1. 3. 119-120; Tak-ṣaka assumed the form of a naked mendi-cant (नग्न श्रमण) and followed Uttaṅka on way; he took the कुण्डलस्, placed by Uttaṅka on the ground, and ran away; when caught by Uttaṅka, Takṣaka assumed his original form and suddenly entered a big hole; on reaching नागलोक he entered his residence (स्वभवन); Uttaṅka went behind him 1. 3. 136-138; when the नागलोक was filled with smoke issuing from the anus of a horse (really god Agni) the confused Takṣaka, frightened by the heat of fire, returned the कुण्डलस् to Uttaṅka 1. 3. 158-159; when asked by the teacher the cause for delay in getting the कुण्डलस्, Uttaṅka told him the hindrance caused by Takṣaka 1. 3. 165-166; angered by this incident Uttaṅka started for Hāstinapura to take revenge on Takṣaka 1. 3. 177. G. Death of Parikṣit: Due to the curse pronounced by Śṛṅgin king Parikṣit was destined to die within a week due to the burning lustre of the eminent serpent Takṣaka 1. 37. 13-14, 19; 1. 46. 8-10; Śṛṅgin's father informed Parikṣit about his impending death at the hands of Takṣaka 1. 38. 19; 1. 46. 12-13; Kāśyapa, an eminent sage (मुनिपुंगव 1. 38. 35), who knew the cure for serpent bites started for Hāstinapura to save Parikṣit from Takṣaka and acquire wealth 1. 38. 31-33; Takṣaka, in disguise of an aged Brāhmaṇa, met Kāśyapa on way and asked him the reason for his hurrying on the way; Kāśyapa told Takṣaka that he wanted to cure Parikṣit when he would be burnt by the fire of Taṣaka's lustre (तेजसा ऽद्य प्रधक्ष्यति); then Takṣaka revealed his identity and told Kāśyapa that he would not be able to save Parikṣit from Takṣaka's bite; Kāśyapa retorted that he was confident about the strength of his science (विद्याबल) 1. 38. 34-39; 1. 46. 15-17; Takṣaka challenged Kāśyapa to bring back to life a न्यग्रोध bitten and burnt by him; this was done by Kāśyapa by his विद्याबल 1. 39. 1-10; astonished, Takṣaka promised to give Kāśyapa all the wealth he desired from Parikṣit, and even more, and begged him to return; he also told Kaśyapa that the curse of the sage was bound to come true, and if Kāśyapa was not able to save Parikṣit he would lose his reputa-tion; having received from Takṣaka the wealth he wanted Kāśyapa turned back 1. 39. 11-19; 1. 46. 18-21; Takṣaka then started for Hās-tinapura; on way he learnt about the arrange-ments made to save Parikṣit with the help of मन्त्रस् and medicines which worked as cures for poison (मन्त्रागदैर् विषहरैः 1. 39. 21); Takṣaka planned to deceive Parikṣit with some trick (मायायोग) and sent to the king serpents in the disguise of hermits with fruits, leaves, and water; when the seventh day since the curse was uttered was about to end Pari-kṣit felt himself secure; he found a small worm in the fruit held by him and said (in joke): “may this small worm turn into Takṣaka and bite me” (कृमिको मां दशत्व् अयम् तक्षको नाम भूत्वा वै 1. 39. 31) and put it on his neck; immediately Takṣaka coiled around the king with his body (भोग) 1. 39. 22-33; the ministers of the king cried and fled; they saw a wonderful (अद्भुत) serpent rising up in the sky 1. 40. 1-3; the whole house was on fire due to the heat of the serpent's poison; Parikṣit died due to the fire (तेजस्) of Takṣaka's poison 1. 40. 4-5; (छद्मेनोपेत्य तक्षकः … दग्धवान् विषवह्निना 1. 46. 22-23). H. Snake-sacrifice: Uttaṅka, embittered by Tak-ṣaka due to the obstacle put by him in Uttaṅka's way, reported to Janamejaya how Takṣaka was responsible for his father's death, and instigated him to burn Takṣaka in the fire of a सर्पसत्र 1. 3. 177-190; when Janamejaya enquired with his mini-sters they told him how his father was killed by Takṣaka (1. 45. 19-28; 1. 46. 1-25); Janamejaya again asked them how they could know the conversation between the Panna-gendra (i. e. Takṣaka) and Kāśyapa when, apparently, it took place in a secluded place in the forest; if satisfied with their expla-nation he would think of the means to kill the serpents (विधास्यामि पन्नगान्तकरीं मतिम्) 1. 46. 26-27; the ministers reported that a man happened to mount the tree before it was burnt by Takṣaka; this man had heard the dialogue between Takṣaka and Kāśyapa; the man too was burnt with the tree; when brought back to life along with the tree the man returned to the town and reported the incident to others 1. 46. 28-31; Janamejaya, satisfied with this account, decided to avenge the death of his father by killing serpents for it was the evil-minded Takṣaka who had offered wealth to Kāśyapa and persuaded him not to go to Hāstina-pura 1. 46. 35-41; Janamejaya wished to know from his house-priest if there was any rite by which he could get Takṣaka and his relatives in the kindled fire; just as Takṣaka had burnt Parikṣit by the fire of his poison (विषाग्नि), so too Janamejaya wished to burn the serpent; priests informed Janamejaya about a rite known as सर्पसत्र, not performed by any one before; thereupon Janamejaya con-sidered Takṣaka as good as burnt in the sacri-ficial fire 1. 47. 3-8; Takṣaka having come to know of the सर्पसत्र went to Indra and sought his shelter; Indra had already propitia-ted Pitāmaha on Takṣaka's behalf and there-fore assured Takṣaka that there was no danger to his life from the fire of सर्पसत्र; Takṣaka then lived happily in Indra's dwelling 1. 48. 14-18; in the meantime when the snake sacrifice was in progress Āstīka appeared at the place of sacrifice where serpents were falling in the fire in large numbers; he praised king Janamejaya; pleased, Janamejaya desired to offer a boon to Āstīka and asked permis-sion of the officiating priests; they gave the permission since Takṣaka was to arrive soon; but the होतृ priest told Janamejaya that Takṣaka was not showing; Janamejaya asked the priests to spare no pains and get Takṣaka quickly; the priests told the king that as the Śāstras informed them and as the Fire narrat-ed to them Takṣaka, out of fear, had taken shelter with Indra 1. 51. 1-5 (यथा शास्त्राणि नः प्राहुर् यथा शंसति पावकः । इन्द्रस्य भवने राजंस् तक्षको भयपीडितः); the king's bard Lohitākṣa, who knew what had transpired (पौराणिको वेदितवान् पुरस्तात् 1. 51. 6), confirmed what the priests had told the king; he said that Indra had asked Takṣaka to stay with him and feel free from any danger from fire; Janamejaya urged his होतृ priest to proceed and the priest with his मन्त्रस् called Indra himself; Indra appeared on the scene with the serpent tucked to his उत्तरीय; Janamejaya asked the priests to make Takṣaka fall in the fire with Indra if he sought shelter in Indra's residence; priests told Jana-mejaya, as they heard a thunderous roar, that Takṣaka was coming under the king's control, they were sure that the serpent was dropped down by Indra and was falling from his lap, the serpent's body was loosened by the मन्त्रस् (मन्त्रविस्रस्तकायः 1. 51. 13) and he had lost consciousness; they permitted Janamejaya to grant a boon to Āstīka since the rite was progressing according to the pres-cription and as Takṣaka was about to fall into the fire; Āstīka chose the boon: “let this sacrificial session come to an end, and let no more serpents fall (into the fire)” (सत्रं ते विरमत्व् एतन् न पतेयुर् इहोर-गाः 1. 51. 17); in vain did Janamejaya try to persuade Āstīka to choose another boon; Janamejaya agreed to stop the session and granted freedom from risk to serpents 1. 51. 6-23; 1. 53. 8; Āstīka admitted that Takṣaka was somehow saved because Jana-mejaya followed the path of truth (and kept his word) (कथंचित् तक्षको मुक्तः सत्य-त्वात् तव पार्थिव) 15. 43. 14; Sūta called it a great miracle of Āstīka that when Tak-ṣaka slipped from Indra's hand, he remained in the sky and did not drop down in the fire; on Śaunaka's query whether Takṣaka's not falling down from the mid-region was due to the fact that the (suitable) मन्त्रस् did not reveal themselves to the priests (मन्त्रग्रामो मनीषिणाम् न प्रत्यभात् 1. 53. 4), Sūta replied that that happened because Āstīka thrice said to the serpent ‘stay’ (तिष्ठ) 1. 53. 1-6, and Takṣaka stayed. I. Upamāna: Bhīṣma with his sharp weapons compared with the big serpent Takṣaka having excess of poison (विषोल्बण) 6. 103. 15; a bow picked up by Aśvatthāman had the lustre of the body of Takṣaka 8. 57. 60. J. Functions and Events: (1) mentioned among the नागस् who, without feeling fatigue, wait on Varuṇa in his सभा; described as marked with banner (पताकिन्), round spots (मण्डलिन्), and hooded (फण-वन्त्) 2. 9. 8, 10; (2) he was among those who received the white snake issuing from the mouth of Balarāma and entering the ocean 16. 5. 14, 12; (3) he was on the side of Arjuna when celestial beings in the sky took sides between Karṇa and Arjuna 8. 63. 36; (4) Ghaṭotkaca and Alaṃbala assumed the shape of Garuḍa and Takṣaka while fighting with each other 7. 149. 26.
तरुणक: Taruṇaka m.: A mythical serpent. Born in the कुल of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, listed by Sūta among those offered in the snake sacrifice of Janamejaya 1. 52. 17, 13; described as ‘swift as wind’ (वातवेग), ‘having excess of poison’ (विषोल्बण) 1. 52. 13.
ताम्रचूड: Tāmracūḍa m.: Name of a cock (?). Given by Aruṇa to Skanda; fighting with feet i. e. with nails (चरणायुध) 9. 45. 46.
ताम्रा: Tāmrā f.: A mythical being. Divine (देवी); she gave birth to five daughters: Kākī, Śyenī, Bhāsī, Dhṛtarāṣṭrī, and Śukī 1. 60. 54.

Tāmrā f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 27, 13; all the rivers listed here are described as mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for citation see Atikṛṣṇā); listed also by Mārkaṇḍeya among the rivers seen by him in the belly of the Bāla (3. 186. 83 = Nārāyaṇa 3. 187. 3) 3. 186. 95; finds place in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 16.
तार: Tāra m.: A monkey-chief. As an ally of Rāma fought with the demon Nikharvaṭa 3. 269. 8; Tāra and others, frightened when Kumbhakarṇa started eating up monkeys, cried aloud; hearing the cry, Sugrīva rushed to their help 3. 271. 5-6; he, along with other monkey-chiefs, surrounded Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa fallen on the ground and bound by Indrajit's arrows 3. 273. 3-4.
तारा: Tārā f.: A female monkey, wife of Vālin. A. Description: Of moon-like face (ताराधिपानना 3. 264. 18, तारापतिमुखी 3. 264. 39), having moon-like lustre (तारा-धिपप्रभा 3. 264. 20). B. Dutiful and intelligent wife: She forbade Vālin from start-ing out of their residence when he heard Sugrīva's loud roar; from the way Sugrīva roared, she feared he had found a protector; since Tārā could understand the meaning of the cries of all beings (सर्वभूतरुतज्ञा 3. 264. 19), Vālin asked her to find out whose protection Sugrīva had secured; after contem-plating for a while she told Vālin incidents beginning with the abduction of Sītā upto Sugrīva's entering into an alliance with Rāma; she also told him about the helpers of Rāma; in the opinion of Tārā all these helpers, intelligent and strong, were capable of destroying Vālin; Vālin misunderstood Tārā's advice and doubted that she secretly loved Sugrīva; he spoke harsh words to her and went out 3. 264. 16-25; in the end Tārā saw Vālin fallen on the ground. C. Marriage with Sugrīva: Sugrīva got Tārā, whose husband was dead, along with the kingdom of Kiṣkindhā 3. 264. 38-39.
तार्क्ष्य: Tārkṣya m.: A mythical bird. [See Garuḍa]
Tārkṣya m. (pl.): Name of a people. Mentioned among those who brought tribute in thousands to Yudhiṣṭhira for his Rājasūya 2. 48. 14.
तार्क्ष्यकेतन: Tārkṣyaketana adj.: One whose banner is marked with Tārkṣya (Garuḍa), epithet of Kṛṣṇa 12. 48. 14. [See Garuḍa]
तित्तिरि: Tittiri m.: A mythical serpent, living in Bhogavatī Purī 5. 101. 13, 1. Son of Surasā and Kaśyapa 5. 101. 4, 17; description 5-7; also listed by Sūta among the sons of Kadrū 1. 31. 15, 2.
त्रिवार: Trivāra m.: A mythical bird, living in the world of Suparṇas 5. 99. 11, 1. Born in the कुल of Vainateya (Garuḍa), in the वंश of Kaśyapa; feeding on serpents; marked with श्रीवत्स, his deity is Viṣṇu; by action a Kṣatriya, not obtaining Brahminhood because indulging in destroying kinsmen 5. 99. 2-8.
तामसास्त्र: Tāmasāstra nt.: Name of a missile. Arjuna struck down with fortitude the Tāmasāstra employed against him apparently by the Rākṣasas 8. 65. 18.
त्रैय्यम्बक: Traiyyambaka (for Traiyambaka ?) adj.: of the missile belonging to Tryambaka, i. e. Śiva. Droṇa knew the use of many missiles, one of these was Traiyyambaka 7. 5. 34. [See Pāśupata]
त्वाष्ट्र: Tvāṣṭra adj.: of the missile belonging to Tvaṣṭṛ. A. Description: great missile (पर-मास्त्र) and ‘killer of the host of enemies’ (अरिसंघघ्न) 7. 18. 14, 11. B. Uses: (1) According to Bhīṣma, only Arjuna and Kṛṣṇa, and no one else, knew the missile of Tvaṣṭṛ and other heavenly missiles 6. 116. 38-39; when employed by Arjuna against the Saṃśaptakas it created thousands of forms so that some of the warriors on the enemy's side looked like Arjuna and Kṛṣṇa; deceived by this delusion, the enemies killed warriors of their own side mistaking them to be Arjuna and Kṛṣṇa; it also destroyed thousands of arrows released by the enemies and killed them 7. 18. 11-15; (2) However, Bhīma himself, like Tvaṣṭṛ, employed this weapon against the demon Alambusa to release thou-sands of arrows to rout the Kaurava army; it destroyed Alambusa's powerful माया (महामाया) and tormented him 7. 83. 34-36; (3) Also employed by Droṇa against Yudhiṣṭhira, but was repelled by the latter 7. 132. 29-30; employed by Droṇa against Arjuna, but was made ineffective by him 7. 163. 28.
तापत्य: Tāpatya nt.: Name of an आख्यान (related to Tapatī). Listed in the contents of the Ādipar-van 1. 2. 87; related to the incidents narra-ted in the अध्यायस् 1. 160-163.
तीर्थयात्रा: Tīrthayātrā f.: Name of the 33rd पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 43, 33, 70. Mentioned while listing the contents of the Āraṇyakaparvan 1. 2. 111; also referred to in 11. 26. 19; related to the अध्यायस् 3. 80-153.
त्रिणाचिकेत: Triṇāciketa m.: Name of a section of the Yajurveda (Tai. Br. 3. 11 ?); in the Mahā-bhārata it occurs as an adj. of a Brāhmaṇa who has studied this section 13. 90. 20. According to an unknown commentator it is a particular section of the Yajurveda (अध्वर्युवेदभागविशेष-), cf. Critical Notes on 13. 90. 20 (p. 1091. 1); so also Kullūka on Manu 3. 185: त्रिणाचिकेतः अध्वर्युवेदभागः, and Nī. on Bom. Ed. 13. 90. 26: त्रिणाचिकेतः त्रिणाचिकेताख्य-मन्त्राध्येता।
त्रिपुरस्य: Tripurasya nipātanam: A narrative (?) from a Purāṇa describing the destruction of the Tripuras (आख्यातं यत्र पौराणं त्रिपुरस्य निपातनम्) 1. 2. 169. Refers to the mythical incidents narrated in the अध्याय 8. 24.
त्रिसुपर्ण: Trisuparṇa m., nt.: Name of a Vedic text; in the Mahābhārata the word occurs as an adj. of a Brāhmaṇa who has studied this text 13. 90. 20. According to Nī. the term applies to the three मन्त्रस् from the Ṛgveda (10. 114. 3-5 which contain the word सुपर्ण) or to those in the Taitt. Ār. 10. 48-50: त्रिसुपर्णं चतुष्कपर्दा युवतिः सुपेषा इति बह्वृचानां मन्त्रत्रयं वा ब्रह्मम् एतु माम् इत्यादि तैत्तिरीयप्रसिद्धं वा on Bom. Ed. 13. 90. 26; the unknown commentator simply says: त्रिसुपर्णः बह्वृचां वेदभाग-वीशेषाध्यायी—see Critical Notes on 13. 90. 20 (p. 1091. 1); so also Kullūka on Manu 3. 185: त्रिसुपर्णो बह्वृचां वेदभागः।
त्रेता: Tretā f., Tretāyuga nt.: Name of the second Yuga among the four Yugas. A. Place among the four Yugas: Second, occurs after Kṛta, hence mentioned after it (पूर्वं कृतयुगं नाम ततस् त्रेतायुगं विभो) 6. 11. 4; 6. 11. 3; 12. 224. 18; 12. 323. 50-51; after Tretā follows Dvāpara (त्रेतानिर्मोक्षसमये द्वापर-प्रतिपादने) 12. 139. 14; hence the junction of these two युगस् is referred to (त्रेता-द्वापरयोः सन्धौ) 1. 2. 3; 12. 139. 13; 12. 326. 78. B. Duration: Mārkaṇḍeya told Yudhiṣṭhira that the duration of the Tretā Yuga was three thousand years, with dawns of three hundred years and twilights of the same duration (त्रीणि वर्षसहस्राणि त्रेतायुगम् इहोच्यते । तस्य तावच्छती संध्या संध्यांशस् च ततः परम् ॥ … संध्यासंध्यांशयोस् तुल्यं प्रमाणम् उपधारय) 3. 186. 19, 21 (for Nī.'s ex-planation of संध्या and संध्यांश, see Kali, Section C); the same duration was told by Vyāsa to Śuka without specifically naming the Yuga but in relation to Kṛta (इतरेषु ससंध्येषु ससंध्यांशेषु च त्रिषु । एकापायेन संयान्ति सहस्राणि शतानि च ॥ ) 12. 224. 20. C. Events: (1) Bhagavān (Nārāyaṇa) told Nārada that in the Tretāyuga, (first), he will be born as Rāma in the family of the Bhṛgus and will destroy the Kṣatriyas; and, (next), when the junction of the Tretā and the Dvāpara will have arrived he will be born as Rāma, son of Daśaratha, to be the king of the world (त्रेतायुगे भविष्यामि रामो भृगुकुलोद्-वहः । क्षत्रं चोत्सादयिष्यामि … ॥ सं-धौ तु समनुप्राप्ते त्रेतायां द्वापर्-अस्य च । रामो दाशर्थिर् भूत्वा भवि-ष्यामि जगत्पतिः ॥ ) 12. 326. 77-78; 1. 2. 3; (2) A being without bodily form informed from the sky (12. 323. 46) Ekata, Dvita and Trita that when the Kṛtayuga had passed and the Tretāyuga of the 7th मन्वन्तर presided over by Manu Vaivasvata will have arrived they will work as helpers of gods for achieving a great purpose (वैवस्वते ऽन्तरे विप्राः प्राप्ते त्रेतायुगे ततः । सुराणां कार्यसिद्ध्यर्थं सहाया वै भविष्यथ) 12. 323. 51; (cf. 12. 326. 79-80); (3) Vyāsa told Yudhiṣṭhira that Karaṃdhama's son (Avikṣit) was born at the commencement of the Tretāyuga—he was glorious, not inferior to Indra, and invin-cible even by the gods 14. 4. 17; (4) Bhīṣma told Yudhiṣṭhira that formerly at the junction of the Tretā and the Dvāpara, a terrible drought, lasting for twelve years, occurred due to the working of the fate (दैवविधि-क्रमात्) 12. 139. 13; when the Tretā was about to end and the Dvāpara was about to set in and when the end of the eon was at hand Indra did not release rain (युगान्ते पर्-युपस्थिते । त्रेतानिर्मोक्षसमये द्वापर-प्रतिपादने ॥ न ववर्ष सहस्राक्षः) 12. 139. 14-15. D. Nārāyaṇa-Kṛṣṇa and Tretā: Bhagavān (Nārāyaṇa) told Mārka-ṇḍeya that his colour in the Tretāyuga was yellow (पीतस् त्रेतायुगे मम) 3. 187. 31; but according to Hanūmant, Acyuta was red in the Tretā (रक्ततां याति चाच्युतः) 3. 148. 23; Bhīṣma told Yudhiṣṭhira that Kṛṣṇa conformed to ज्ञान in the Tretā (त्रेताकाले ज्ञानम् अनुप्रपन्नः) 13. 143. 9 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 13. 158. 10: ज्ञानम् अकर्तव्यकोटेर् अपि उपस्थानात् त्रेतायां विवेक आसीत्). E. King and Tretā: When the king observes दण्डनीति only in three parts and leaves out the fourth, the Tretā-yuga sets in; the place of the fourth part is then made up by what is inauspicious and this part gets associated with the other three, hence the earth has to be ploughed for the growth of the plants (दण्डनीत्या यदा राजा त्रीन् अंशान् अनुवर्तते । चतुर्थम् अंशम् उत्सृज्य तदा त्रेता प्रवर्तते ॥ अशुभस्य चतुर्थांशस् त्रीन् अंशान् अनुवर्तते । कृष्ट-पच्यैव पृथिवी भवन्त्योषध्यस् तथा ॥ ) 12. 70. 14-15; (पादोनेनापि धर्मेण गच्-छेत् त्रेतायुगे तथा) 12. 259. 32; a king is the cause of the Tretā (as also of the other three Yugas) (त्रेतायाः … । … राजा भवति कारणम्) 5. 130. 16 = 12. 70. 25; (also cf. राजा कालस्य कारणम् 12. 70. 6 = 5. 130. 15); Tretā, like the other three Yugas, depends on the conduct of the king and hence the king is called a Yuga (राजवृत्तानि सर्वाणि राजैव युगम् उच्यते) 12. 92. 6; (राज-मूलानि सर्वाणि) 12. 139. 10; a king obtains heaven, but not endlessly, because he intro-duces Tretā (त्रेतायाः करणाद् राजा स्वर्गं नात्यन्तम् अश्नुते) 5. 130. 17 = 12. 70. 26; description of the people in the Tretā in the absence of दण्डनीति 12. 65. 24-27; F. Tretā and धर्म: In the Tretāyuga Dharma loses one of its four feet (तत्र (i. e. त्रेतायुगे) पादचतुर्थो वै धर्म्-अस्य न भविष्यति) 12. 327. 74; (पादेन ह्रसते धर्मः) 3. 148. 22-23; in the Tretā, Dharma is established in three parts and the remaining one part is affected by अधर्म (अधर्मपादविद्धस् तु त्रिभिर् अंशैः प्रतिष्ठितः । त्रेतायाम्) 3. 188. 11; also of 12. 259. 32; in the Tretā and the other two following Yugas the धर्म is displaced from tradition successively by one quarter and the अधर्म is on increase due to thefts, falsehood and deceit (इतरेष्व् (i. e. युगेषु) आगमाद् धर्मः पादशस् त्व् अवरोप्यते । चौरिकानृतमायाभिर् अधर्मश् चोपचीयते) 12. 224. 23; the धर्मस् in the Tretā were different from those in the Kṛta 12. 224. 26 = 12. 252. 8; ज्ञान was considered to be the best धर्म for the Tretā (त्रेतायां ज्ञानम् उत्तमम्) 12. 224. 27; Hanūmant told Bhīma that times in the different Yugas were different 3. 148. 6; Vyāsa told his son Śuka that he had heard that the study of the Vedas decreased in every following Yuga and so also the benefit derived by people from the Veda (वेदवादाश् चानुयुगं ह्रसन्तीति च नः श्रुतम् । … वेदस्यैव च यत् फलम्) 12. 224. 25; the Sātvata धर्म, which flourished in the Kṛtayuga of the fourth birth of Brah-man (12. 336. 25), disappeared when the Tretā returned (ततः सो ऽन्तर्दधे भूयः प्राप्ते त्रेतायुगे पुनः) 12. 336. 35; but in the seventh birth of Brahman (12. 336. 44) the same Sātvata धर्म was taught by Vivasvān to Manu 12. 326. 47; according to Mārkaṇḍeya, however, the धर्म for the Kṛta, the Tretā and the Dvāpara was the same 3. 189. 13. G. Tretā and the sacrifice: There were no sacrifices in the Kṛtayuga, but they all, very strong, collected together appeared in the Tretā and be-came controllers of those that move (living beings) and those that do not (non-living beings) (त्रेतायुगे विधिस् त्व् एषां यज्ञानां न कृते युगे … त्रेतायां तु समस्तास् ते प्रादुरासन् महाबलाः । संयन्तारः स्थावराणां जङ्गमानां च सर्वशः ॥ त्रेतायां संहता ह्य् एते यज्ञाः … ) 12. 224. 62, 64, 65 (Nī., however, on Bom. Ed. 12. 232. 34: त्रेतायां धर्मे नृणां स्वतः प्रवृत्त्यभावात् तत्र संयन्तारो धर्म-शास्तारो वेदाश् च संहता यज्ञाद्यनुष्ठा-पनाय सन्नद्धा आसन्); Bhagavān (Nārā-yana) told the gods that the three Vedas will rule the Tretāyuga and then the animals, consecrated for the sacrifice, will be killed (ततस् त्रेतायुगं नाम त्रयी यत्र भवि-ष्यति । प्रोक्षिता यत्र पशव वधं प्राप्स्यन्ति वै मखे । ) 12. 327. 74; (त्रेताम् अपि निबोध त्वम् यस्मिन् सत्रं प्रवर्तते) 3. 148. 22; (ततो यज्ञाः प्र-वर्तन्ते धर्माश् च विविधाः क्रियाः । त्रेतायां भावसंकल्पाः क्रियादानफलो-दयाः ॥ ) 3. 148. 24 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 149. 23: सत्रं यज्ञक्रिया रजोमिश्रत्वात्; on 3. 149. 25: भावसंकल्पाः भावो भावना क्रिया अहम् अनेन कर्मणा इदं फलं अनेन प्रकारेण करिष्यामीत्य् एवंरूपा तद्विषय एव संकल्पो येषाम्); Vyāsa told Śuka that at the commencement of the Tretā the Vedas and the sacrifices are complete in form (त्रेतादौ सकला वेदा यज्ञा वर्णाश्रामास् तथा) 12. 230. 14; (also cf. Maheśvara (Viṣṇu) recommending the performance of sacrifices for the benefit of gods, and the gods, on their part, sustaining the worlds in the Yugas (not named) other than the Kṛta 12. 327. 53-60). H. Nature of the Tretāyuga: Hanūmant told Bhīma that the times in the Tretā were different from those in the Kṛta (अन्यः कृतयुगे कालस् त्रेतायां द्वापरे ऽपरः) 3. 148. 6; Hanū-mant then described to Bhīma the condition of the world in the Tretāyuga 3. 148. 22-25 (men are truthful (सत्यप्रवऋत्ताश् च नराः), they do not deviate from the path of धर्म, are given to the practice of austerities and to giving gifts); the Tretāyuga also described by Saṃjaya to Dhṛtarāṣṭra (Kṣatriyas are long-lived, they are great warriors, excellent archers in war, brave and emperors) 6. 11. 10 (जायन्ते क्षत्रियाः शूरास् त्रेतायां चक्र-वर्तिनः); according to Mārkaṇḍeya the condition of धर्म in the Tretā is not different from the one in the Kṛta described by him (एष धर्मः कृतयुगे त्रेआयाम्) 3. 189 13; the ascetics in the Tretā, who are steady in the सत्त्व गुण, have no doubt whatever whether पुरुष, दैव or स्वभाव is the cause of a man's success in his activities; they see no distinction, as same people for want of judgement do, between them (पौरुषं कारणं केचिद् आहुः कर्मसु मानवाः । दविअम् एके प्रशंसन्ति स्वभावं चापरे जनाः ॥ … त्रयम् एतत् पृथग्भूतम् अविवेकं तु केचन । … कर्मस्था विषमं ब्रूयुः सत्त्वस्थाः समदर्शिनः ॥ त्रेतायां … तपस्विनः … ) 12. 230. 4, 6-7; in the Tretā, as in the Kṛta, people could get progeny by mere thought and did not have to cohabit for this purpose (तत्र त्रेतायुगे काले सं-कल्पाज् जायते प्रजा । न ह्य् अभूत् मैथुनो धर्मस् तेषाम् अपि नराधिप ॥ ) 12. 200. 36; evil tribes like the Talavaras, the Andhrakas and others in the south and the Yaunas (Yavanas), the Kāmbojas and others in the north, unlike in the Kṛtayuga, begin to roam about on the surface of the earth from the Tretāyuga onwards (नैते कृतयुगे तात चरन्ति पृथिवीम् इमाम् । त्रेताप्रभृति वर्तन्ते ते जना भरतर्-षभ ॥ ) 12. 200. 42. I. Span of life: Vyāsa told Śuka that people in each suc-ceeding Yuga lived a quarter years less than those in the Kṛtayuga who lived for four hundred years, i. e. in the Tretā they lived for three hundred years (चतुर्वर्ष-शतायुषः । कृते त्रेतादिष्व् एतेषां पादशो ह्रसते वयः) 12. 224. 24; Vyāsa had heard that life gradually decreased in each succes-sive Yuga (अनुयुगं ह्रसन्तीति च नः श्रुतम् । आयूंषि) 12. 224. 25; the same thing was told by Mārkaṇḍeya to Yudhi-ṣṭhira (आयुर् वीर्यम् अथो बुद्धिर् बलं तेजश् च पाण्डव । मनुष्याणाम् अनुयुगं ह्रसतीति निबोध मे) 3. 188. 13; however, Saṃjaya, told Dhṛtarāṣṭra that people lived for three thousand years in the Tretā (आयुः-संख्या … संख्याता राजसत्तम । तथा त्रीणि सहस्राणि त्रेतायां मनुजाधिप ॥ ) 6. 11. 5-6 (apparently, in Saṃjaya's narra-tion, there is confusion between the dura-tion of the Tretāyuga (cf. section B. above) and the life expectancy of the people in this Yuga). J. Simile: The region where the river Narmadā (f.) passes along the Vaiḍūrya mountain (m.) is compared with the conjunction of the Tretā (f.) and the Dvāpara (m) (वैडूर्यपर्वतं दृष्ट्वा नर्मदाम् अवतीर्य च । सन्धिर् एष नर-श्रेष्ठ त्रेताया द्वापरस्य च ॥ ) 3. 121. 18-19. K. Name of Sūrya: Tretā appears as the 47th name among the hundred and eight names of Sūrya taught by Dhaumya to Yudhiṣṭhira 3. 3. 22. [The words Kṛta, Tretā and Dvāpara occurring in 5. 140. 7-15 are wrongly interpreted by Nī. (Bom. Ed. 5. 142. 7-15) as names of the three Yugas and not as the names of the throws of dice in a dice-game].
तपोद: Tapoda nt. (pl.): Name of a तीर्थ। Situated in the Rājagṛha; by bathing there one enjoys like Kākṣīvant (उपस्पृश्य तपोदेषु काक्षीवान् इव मोदते) 3. 82. 89; by eating a part of the daily food offered to the Yakṣiṇī there a pure person, by the grace of the Yakṣiṇī, is freed of the sin of killing an embryo (यक्षिण्या नैत्यकं तत्र प्राश्नीत पुरुषः शुचिः । यक्षिण्यास् तु प्रसादेन मुच्यते भ्रूणहत्यया) 3. 82. 90; (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 84. 105: नित्यकं नैवेद्यं नैत्यकं च तद् एव).
तपोदान: Tapodāna nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Listed in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 19, 2.
तमसा: Tamasā f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 30, 13; all the rivers listed by Saṃjaya are said to be mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for citation see Atikṛṣṇā); also listed by Mārkaṇḍeya among the rivers which are famous as mothers of sacrificial hearths, i. e. on the banks of which sacrifices were per-formed (एता नद्यस् तु धिष्ण्यानां मातरो याः प्रकीर्तिताः) 3. 212. 23-24 (for Nī. see Kapilā).
तरन्तुक: Tarantuka nt.: Perhaps also a तीर्थ named after the gate-keeper Yakṣa of that name. Situated on the river Sarasvatī; sacred to Arantuka, the chief of the Yakṣas 3. 81. 42; by living there for one night one gets the fruit of giving a thousand cows (ततो गच्छेत धर्मज्ञ द्वारपालं तरन्तु-कं । तत्रोष्य रजनीम् एकाम् अग्निष्टोम-फलं लभेत् ॥ ) 3. 81. 13; by bathing there one gets the fruit of an Agniṣṭoma sacrifice 3. 81. 42; along with the Arantuka तीर्थ and other तीर्थस् it forms the boun-dary of the Kurukṣetra-Samantapañcaka (तरन्तुकारन्तुकयोर् यद् अन्तरम् … एतत् कुरुक्षेत्रसमन्तपञ्चकम्) 3. 81. 178 = 9. 52. 20.
ताम्रपर्णी: Tāmraparṇī f.: Name of a river. Situated in the south 3. 86. 1; gods prac-tised austerities there in an आश्रम wishing something great for themselves (यत्र देवैस् तपस् तप्तं महद् इच्छद्भिर् आश्रमे) 3. 86. 11-12.
ताम्रारुण: Tāmrāruṇa nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। One who has practised chastity and is composed (ब्रह्मचारी समाहितः) he, by visiting this तीर्थ, obtained the reward of a horse sacrifice and went to the world of Śakra (Indra) 3. 82. 133.
ताम्रावती: Tāmrāvatī f.: Name of a river. Listed by Mārkaṇḍeya among the rivers which are proclaimed as mothers of fire-hearths i. e. on the banks of which sacrifices were offered (एता नद्यस् तु धिष्ण्यानां मातरो याः प्रकीर्तिताः) 3. 212. 22 (for Nī. see Kapilā).
तीर्थकोटि: Tīrthakoṭi f.: Name of a तीर्थ। Situated near the Maheśvarapada (तत्र कोटिस् तु तीर्थानाम्) 3. 82. 103-104; described as famous (विश्रुता) 3. 82. 104; they were carried away by a wicked demon in the form of a tortoise, but were brought back by powerful Viṣṇu 3. 82. 104; by bathing there (तत्राभिषेकं कुर्वाणस् तीर्थकोट्याम्) one obtained the fruit of a Puṇḍarīka sacrifice and went to the world of Viṣṇu 3. 82. 105. [See Koṭitīrtha]
तुङ्गक: Tuṅgaka nt.: Name of a forest. A. Past events: (1) The sage Sāras-vata, the son of Aṅgiras, formerly taught there the lost Vedas while he was sitting on the upper garments of the great sages; when his pupils pronounced properly the syllable ‘ॐ’ whatever each one of them had learnt before came back to him (तुङ्गकारण्यम् आसाद्य ब्रह्मचारि जितेन्द्रियः । वेदान् अध्यापयत् तत्र ऋषिः सारस्वतः पुरा ॥ तत्र वेदान् प्रनष्टांस् तु मुनेर् अङ्गि-रसः सुतः । उपविष्टो महर्षीणाम् उत्तरी-येषु भारत ॥ ओंकारेण यथान्यायं सम्यगुच्चारितेन च । येन यत् पूर्वम् अभ्यस्तं तत् तस्य समुपस्थितम् ॥ ) 3. 83. 43-45; (2) many sages and gods like Varuṇa, Agni, Prajāpati, Hari-Nārāyaṇa, Mahādeva (had assembled there); Pitāmaha (Brahmadeva) appointed Bhṛgu to perform a sacrifice (भृगुं नियोजयाम् आस याजनार्-थे); the blessed (Bhṛgu) then established again fire for the sages according to the rites; the gods and sages, satisfied by their shares of the clarified butter, went happily to the three worlds 3. 83. 46-49. B. Holiness: The sin of every one, whether man or woman, who enters the Tuṅgaka forest is destroyed; a wise person who is controlled and subsists on limited food (धीरो नियतो नियताशनः), if he lives there for a month he will go to-the Brahmaloka and will purify his family 3. 83. 50-51.
तुङ्गवेणा: Tuṅgaveṇā f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratvarṣa; its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 26, 13; all the rivers listed here are said to be mothers of the uni-verse and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for citation see Atikṛṣṇā).
तूष्णींगङ्गा: Tūṣṇīṃgaṅgā f.: Name of a river. The river is mentioned among those holy places by visiting which the high-souled persons, who have observed vows, go to the Goloka (गवां विमाणे 13. 105. 44), after they assume heavenly forms, wear heavenly garlands, become auspicious and rich in holy fragrance 13. 105. 46, 48 (for citation see Karatoyinī).
तृणबिन्दुसरस्: Tṛṇabindusaras nt.: Name of a lake. Situated near the Kāmyaka forest (काम्यकं … तृणबिन्दुसरः प्रति) 3. 244. 13.
त्रसामन्या: Trasāmanyā f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 30, 13; all the rivers listed here are said to be mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for citation see Atikṛṣṇā).
त्रिकूट: Trikūṭa1 m.: Name of a mountain (?) The eyebrow of Bhīma forming three peaks on his forehead looked like the river Gaṅgā flowing in three courses on the Trikūṭa (or on the three peaks of a mountain ?) (ट्रिशिखां भ्रुकुटीं चास्य ददृशुः सर्व-पार्थिवाः । ललाटस्थां त्रिकूटस्थां गङ्गां त्रिपथगाम् इव) 2. 39. 11. [See Trikūṭavant and Triśṛṅga]

Trikūṭa2 m.: Name of a mountain in the Laṅkā. Rāvaṇa crossed it (and the Kāla-parvata) before he reached the ocean while he was on his way to Gokarṇa 3. 261. 53; Laṅkā of Rāvaṇa was located in the valley of the mountain Trikūṭa beyond the ocean (लङ्का चास्य महापुरी । दृष्टा पारे समुद्-रस्य त्रिकूटगिरिकन्दरे) 3. 266. 55.
त्रिकूटवत्: Trikūṭavant m.: Name of a mountain. Listed by Brahmadeva among the mountains described as the kings of moun-tains (एते पर्वतराजानः) 14. 43. 4. (Are these mountains also to be looked upon as having an excess of the मध्यम गुण i. e. of the quality of रजस् ? cf. 14. 43. 1 and Nī. on Bom. Ed. 14. 43. 1: मध्यमो गुणः रजोगुणप्रधानः). [See Trikūṭa1 and Triśṛṅga]
त्रिकूटवन्त्: Trikūṭavant m.: Name of a mountain. Listed by Brahmadeva among the mountains described as the kings of moun-tains (एते पर्वतराजानः) 14. 43. 4. (Are these mountains also to be looked upon as having an excess of the मध्यम गुण i. e. of the quality of रजस् ? cf. 14. 43. 1 and Nī. on Bom. Ed. 14. 43. 1: मध्यमो गुणः रजोगुणप्रधानः). [See Trikūṭa1 and Triśṛṅga]
त्रिगङ्ग: Trigaṅga nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। By giving offerings here to gods and manes according to the rites one is glori-fied in the world obtained by pious men (पुण्यलोके महीयते) 3. 82. 25; if one gives here offerings (to gods and manes) he enjoys सुधा when he is born again (in the world of the pious ?) (सुधां वै लभते भोक्तुं यो नरो जायते पुनः) 13. 26. 15.
त्रिदिवा: Tridivā f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya twice among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 16, 17, 13; all the rivers listed here are said to the mothers of the universe and very strong (for citation See Atikṛṣṇā); finds mention in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 22, 2.
त्रिविष्टप: Triviṣṭapa nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Described as famous in the three worlds (त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतम्) 3. 81. 70; situated near the holy river Vaitaraṇī 3. 81. 70; by bathing in this तीर्थ and by worshipping god Śūlapāṇi Vṛṣadhvaja (Śiva), one's self is cleansed of all evils and one attains the highest state (after death) (सर्वपापविशुद्-धात्मा गच्छेत परमां गतिम्) 3. 81. 71.
त्रिशूलखात: Triśūlakhāta nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Situated near the rivers (?) Sugandhā, Śatakumbhā and Pañcayajñā; by bathing there (तत्राभिषेकं कुर्वीत) and by being devoted to the worship of gods and manes, one obtains without doubt the status of a Gaṇapati after death (पितृदेवार्चने रतः । गाणप्त्यं स लभते देहं त्यक्त्वा न संशयः) 3. 82. 9-10.
त्रिशूलपाणेः: Triśūlapāṇeḥ sthānam nt.: Name of a sacred place. Situated near the river Devikā; described as famous in the three worlds (त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतम्) 3. 80. 111; by bathing in Devikā and by worshipping Maheśvara (Śiva) there and by offering a चरु according to one's ability (यथाशक्ति चरुं तत्र निवेद्य), one obtains the reward of a sacrifice that grants all wishes (सर्वकामसमृद्धस्य यज्ञस्य लभते फलम्) 3. 80. 112.
त्रिशृङ्ग: Triśṛṅga m.: Name of a mountain. Described as an excellent mountain (पर्वतोत्तम) 8. 11. 8; Aśvatthāman with the three arrows shot at him by Bhīma and stuck in the forehead looked like the Triśṛṅga in the rainy season 8. 11. 7-8; (the three holy peaks (शृङ्गाणि त्रीणि पुण्याणि) on the Ārcīka mountain, pointed out by Lomaśa, identical with the Triśṛṅga ? Yudhiṣṭhira was advised by Lomaśa to go around them and bathe in the three streams flowing there) (सर्वाण्य् अनुपरिक्रम्य यथाकामन् उप-स्पृश) 3. 125. 15; (Nī., however, on Bom. Ed. 3. 125. 18: त्रीणि शृङ्गाणीति प्राग्व्या-ख्यातरीत्या (cf. his comm. on 3. 82. 38) त्रि-कोणं वाराणसीक्षेत्रम् । ). [See Trikūṭa1, Trikūṭavant]
तक्षशिला: Takṣaśilā f.: Name of a city. Janamejaya, after instructing his bro-thers to act as told by his chosen Purohita Somaśravas, marched on Takṣaśilā and brought it under his control 1. 3. 18; when Uttaṅka went to Hāstinapura to incite Janamejaya to take revenge on Takṣaka, the latter had already returned victorious from Takṣaśilā 1. 3. 179; Janamejaya, after completing the सर्पसत्र, returned from Takṣaśilā to Hāstinapura (ततः समाप-याम् आसुः कर्म तत् तस्य याजकाः । … ततः तक्षशिलायाः स पुनर् आयाद् गजाह्वयम्) 18. 5. 27, 29.
तण्डूलिकाश्रम: Taṇḍūlikāśrama m.: Name of an आश्रम। After visiting the तीर्थ called Jambū-mārga one should visit Taṇḍūlikāśrama; he is thereby not affected by distress and is honoured in heaven (न दुर्गतिम् अवा-प्नोति स्वर्गलोके च पूज्यते) 3. 80. 62.
तण्डेर्: *Taṇḍer āśramaḥ m.: The आश्रम of Taṇḍi. After receiving a boon from god Śiva, Taṇḍi returned to his आश्रम and narrated one thousand and eight names of Śarva (Śiva) to Upamanyu 13. 16. 12, 71-72; 13. 17. 29.
तृणसोमाग्नेर्: Tṛṇasomāgner āśramaḥ m.: An आश्रम established by Tṛṇasomāgni. Tṛṇasomāgni was the pupil of Agastya (आश्रमो ऽगस्त्यशिष्यस्य) 3. 86. 14; situa-ted in the south (3. 86. 1); on the moun-tain Devasabha: it was near the Vaiḍūrya mountain and the आश्रम of Agastya 3. 86. 14-15; described as holy (पुण्य) and full of fruits and roots (संपन्नफलमूलवन्त्) 3. 86. 14.
त्रिपुर: Tripura nt.: Name of the three cities of the three Asuras. A. Creation: Created by Asura Maya for the three sons of Tāraka, viz. Tārākṣa (or Tārakākṣa), Kamalākṣa and Vidyunmālin; the cities were obtained by them as a boon from Pitāmaha; one of the three cities was made of gold, the other of silver, and the third of iron; they moved in them respectively in heaven, in mid region, and with the third, stationed on wheels, on the earth; (काञ्चनं दिवि तत्रासीद् अन्तरिक्षे च राजतम् । आय-सं चाभवद् भूमौ चक्रस्थं पृथिवी-पते ॥ ) 8. 24. 4, 10, 13-15 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 8. 33. 18, however, चक्रस्थं आज्ञावशं यथेष्टसंचारीत्य् अर्थः); (according to 13. 145. 24, however, all the three cities were in heaven (असुराणां पुराण्य् आसंस् त्रीणि वीर्यवतां दिवि । आयसं राजतं चैव सौवर्णम् अपरं तथा ॥ ). B. Des-cription: Inaccessible (दुर्ग) 8. 24. 20; guarded by Daityas and Dānavas (दैत्य-दानवरक्षित) 8. 24. 114. C. Charac-teristics: (1) The three cities were supposed to come together and be united at the end of one thousand years; if some prominent god were then to strike the cities with a single arrow, the god would be death for them (समागतानि चैतानि यो हन्याद् भगवंस् तदा । एकेषुणा देववरः स नो मृत्युर् भविष्यति ॥ ) 8. 24. 11-12; (2) Whatever was desired by a person who had taken shelter in the Tripuras (त्रिपुरसं-श्रयः) was procured for him by Maya with the help of his माया (तस्मै कामं मयस् तं तं विदधे मायया तदा) 8. 24. 22; (3) Hari, the son of Tārakākṣa, obtained as a boon from Pitāmaha, a well in their पुर (वापी भवतु नः पुरे); if any demon, wounded by weapons, was thrown into this well, he arose from it stronger; if a dead demon was thrown into it, he came back alive (मृतानां जीवनीम्); forti-fied with this well the denizens of the Tripuras oppressed all the three worlds 8. 24. 23-27. D. Mythological event: Since Indra was unable to shatter the Tri-puras, although he used all his weapons against them, gods approached Rudra and requested him to destroy the demons and their cities; Śiva then burnt the three पुरस् together with the demons, using gods as chariot (देवान् रथवरम् कृत्वा), god Viṣṇu as arrow, Agni as tip of the arrow (शल्य), Yama as hind part of the arrow (पुङ्ख); Śiva's arrow had three joints and three heads (to correspond to the three पुरस् ?) (त्रिपर्वणा त्रिशल्येन … शरेण) 13. 145. 24-29; Śiva's chariot was driven in the direction of the Tripuras by Pitāmaha; Śiva employed his Pāśupata missile on his bow and thought of the Tripuras (त्रिपुरं समचिन्तयत्) 8. 24. 115; at the appointed time the three पुरस् came together and were united; when they came in his view, Śiva shot his arrow which burnt the Tripuras and the demons in them and threw them in the western ocean; thus Maheśvara, wishing well for the three worlds, burnt the Tripuras and the demons 8. 24. 114-121; this report in the Karṇa-parvan of the downfall of the Tripuras which was according to the account in the Purāṇas is referred to in the Anukramaṇī-parvan (आख्यातं यत्र पौराणं त्रिपु-रस्य निपातनम्) 1. 2. 169. E. Similies: (1) The town Saubha, when cut into two by the Sudarśanacakra of Kṛṣṇa, fell down as did the Tripura when tossed up by the arrow of Maheśvara (महेश्वरशरो-द्धूतं पपात त्रिपुरं यथा) 3. 23. 34; (2) Aśvatthāman, after burning an अक्षौ-हिणी army of the demons (of Ghaṭotkaca), shone as Maheśvara formerly did in heaven after burning the Tripura (पुरेव तृइपुरं दग्ध्वा दिवि देवो महेश्वरः) 7. 131. 98; (3) The same simile is found when Karṇa killed the demons (of Ghaṭotkaca) 7. 150. 83.
तङ्गण: Taṅgaṇa m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada and its people. A. Location: There seem to be two Taṅgaṇas: northern and southern: (1) They are said to have lived in the large kingdom of Subāhu on Himālaya (सुबाहोर् विषयं महत् … किराततङ्गणाकीर्णम् … हिमवत्य् अमरैर् जुष्टम्) 3. 141. 24-25; they lived in the region between the mountains Meru and Mandara and along the river Śailodā (मेरुमन्दरयोर् मध्ये शैलोदाम् अभितो नदीम्) 2. 48. 2; (2) Listed by Saṃjaya among the southern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of the Bhāratavarṣa (अथापरे दक्षिणा जनपदा … ) 6. 10. 56, 5; (तङ्गणाः परतङ्गणाः) 6. 10. 63; designated as जनपद also in 6. 46. 50. B. Characte-ristic: They enjoyed the pleasing shadow of कीचक and वेणु types of bamboos (ये ते कीचकवेणूनां छायां रम्याम् उपासते) 2. 48. 2. C. Description: Strong, very strong (बलिन्) 8. 51. 19; (अतिबल) 8. 5. 18; fierce (उग्र) and of cruel deeds (क्रूरकर्मन्) 8. 51. 18; furious, expert in battles, firm-fisted (संरंभिणो युद्ध-शौण्डा … दृब्धपाणयः) 8. 51. 19; diffi-cult to be won (दुर्जय) 8. 5. 18; no one except Arjuna could conquer them (न शक्या युधि निर्जेतुं त्वद् अन्येन परं-तप) 8. 51. 20. D. Epic events: (1) King of Taṅgaṇas brought lumps of gold of the पिपीलिक variety, given as boon by ants (?), to be measured by द्रोणस्, as tribute for the Rājasūya; they were stopped at the gate (ते वै पिपीलिकं नाम वरदत्तं पिपीलिकैः । जातरूपं द्रोणमेयम् अहार्षुः पुञ्जशो नृपाः … द्वारि तिष्ठन्ति वारिताः) 2. 48. 3-4, 7; (2) Subdued by the fear of the sharp edge of the weapons of Pāṇḍavas, they attended the Rājasūya and acted as servers at meals (शस्त्रतेजो-भयार्दितान् … तङ्गणान् … यज्ञे ते पऋइ-वेषकान्) 3. 48. 18, 21-22; (3) Karṇa had once defeated them and were made to pay tribute (चक्रे बलिभृतः पुरा) 8. 5. 18; (4) Mentioned among those who joined the Kauravas for the sake of Duryodhana 8. 51. 18, 20; (5) On the second day of war, the Taṅgaṇas on the side of the Pāṇḍavas were stationed at the right wing (दक्षिणं पक्षम्) of the Krauñcāruṇa vyūha 6. 46. 39) of the Pāṇḍavas 6. 46. 49; (6) On the fourteenth day of war, Taṅgaṇas on the side of the Kauravas, led by Duryodhana, attacked Sātyaki; Sātyaki repulsed with ञाराच arrows the attack of Taṅgaṇas who fought with iron weapons and शूलस् (अयोहस्तैः शूल-हस्तैः) 7. 97. 14, 39; (7) On the sixteenth day of war, Pāṇḍya killed many of them who rode on horsebacks and fought with शक्ति, प्रास and bows and arrows (सशक्तिप्रासतूणीरान् अश्वारोहान्) 8. 15. 9; (8) One of the countries visited by the Aśvamedha horse was Taṅgaṇa (किरातान् अथ तङ्गणान्) 14. 84. 4.
तरतोय: Taratoya m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of the Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जन-पदान् निबोध गदतो मम) 6. 10. 37, 5; (तीरग्राहास् तरतोया … ) 6. 10. 51.
तरल: Tarala m. (pl.): Name of a people. Karṇa had once defeated Tarala warriors in battle and made them pay tribute (तरलान् … यो जित्वा समरे वीरश् चक्रे बलिभृतः पुरा) 8. 5. 20.
तलवन: Talavana m. (pl.): Name of a people. Sahadeva in his expedition to the south (2. 28. 1, 8, 37) subjugated them just by sending messengers and made them pay tribute for the Rājasūya (अन्ध्रांस् तल-वनांश् चैव … दूतैर् एव वशे चक्रे करं चैनान् अदापयत्) 2. 28. 48-49.
तामर: Tāmara m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the southern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of the Bhāratavarṣa (अथापरे जनपदा दक्षिणा … ) 6. 10. 56; (तामरा हंस-मार्गाश् च) 6. 10. 68.
ताम्र: Tāmra nt.: Name of a द्वीप। Sahadeva in his expedition to the south (2. 28. 1, 8, 37) subjugated it just by sending messengers and made the people pay tribute for the Rājasūya (द्वीपं ताम्राह्वयं चैव) 2. 28. 46-47.
ताम्रलिङ्गक: Tāmraliṅgaka m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of the Bhāratavarṣa 6. 10. 37, 5; (विदेहास् ताम्रलीङ्गकाः) 6. 10. 55.
ताम्रलिप्त: Tāmralipta(ka) m. (pl.): Name of a people. A. Characteristic: Skilled in fighting while riding elephants (गजयोधिनः । … ताम्रलिप्तकाः ॥ … गजयुद्धेषु कुशलाः) 8. 17. 2-3. B. Epic events: (1) Their kings brought fine cloth, silk material, thin cotton cloth and mantles as tribute for Yudhiṣṭhira's Rājasūya, but they were not allowed to enter the sacrificial enclosure by the gate-keepers; on being asked to give more, each one of them gave a thousand well-bred elephants of the Kāmyaka lake, huge like mountains, having long tusks, gold girdles, lotus-coloured, covered with painted cloth and protected by armours, always in rut yet patient; then they were allowed to enter the gate (ताम्रलिप्ताः … दुकूलं कौशिकं चैव पत्रोर्णं प्रावरान् अपि) 2. 48. 17; (ईषा-दन्तान् हेमकक्षान् पद्मवर्णान् कुथा-वृतान् । शैलाभान् नित्यमत्तांश् च अभितः काम्यकं सरः ॥ दत्त्वैकैको दशशतान् कुञ्जरान् कवचावृतान् । क्षमावतः कुली-नांश् च) 2. 48. 19-20; (2) On the four-teenth day of war, Sātyaki, while advanc-ing to meet Arjuna had to fight with them who were armed with various weapons (ताम्रलिप्तकाः … विविधायुधपाणयः) 7. 95. 13; (3) On the sixteenth day of war, their elephant-riders (गजयोधिनः) attacked Dhṛṣṭadyumna and showered on him arrows of the नाराच type and तोम-रस् 8. 17. 2, 4; on the same day they also attacked Nakula with arrows and तोमरस् (ताम्रलिप्तकाः । शरतोमरवर्षाणि विमुञ्-चन्तो जिघांसवः) 8. 17. 20, 21.
तालजङ्घ: Tālajaṅgha m. (pl.): Name of some Kṣatriyas. Past events: (1) King Sagara extir-pated them along with Haihayas 3. 104. 7; (2) King Bakula of the Tālajaṅghas was one of the sixteen kings who completely annihilated their kinsmen, friends and relatives (ये समुच्चिच्छिदुर् ज्ञातीन् सुहृदश् च सबान्धवान्) 5. 72. 13, 11; (3) To illustrate that the lustre and strength of the Kṣatriyas was pacified when they faced Brāhmaṇas, Bhīṣma mentioned that the Bhṛgus had conquered Tālajaṅghas 13. 34. 15-16; Aurva (a Bhārgava) alone destroyed a large number of Tālajaṅgha Kṣatriyas (तालजङ्घं महत् क्षत्रम् और्वेणैकेन नाशितम्) 13. 138. 11.
तालचर: Tālacara m. (pl.): Name of a people. Kṛṣṇa told Karṇa that if the were to join the Pāṇḍavas, Tālacaras would be in the forefront of his march (पुरोगमाश् च ते सन्तु … तालचराश् चैव) 5. 138. 25.
तित्तिर: Tittira m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada and its people. A. Special feature: Famous for its horses (see B. Epic events, No. 2); B. Epic events: (1) On the second day of war, the Tittira warriors, along with many others, were stationed at the right wing of the Krauñcāruṇavyūha (6. 46. 39; Krauñca 6. 47. 1) of the Pāṇḍavas (तित्तिराश् चैव … एते जनपदा राजन् दक्षिणं पक्षम् आश्रिताः) 6. 46. 50; (2) On the eighth day of war, Irāvān confronted the cavalry of Śakuni and Hārdikya (Kṛtavarman) with his Tittira-bred horses which were swift, having the speed of wind, decorated with gold, provided with armour and well-equipped (ये चापरे तित्तिरजा जवना वातर-ंहसः) 6. 86. 4-5; for further description of horses see 6. 86. 15-16.
तिलक: Tilaka m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of the Bhāratavarṣa 6. 10. 37, 5; (तिलकाः पारसीकाश् च) 6. 10. 51.
तीरग्राह: Tīragrāha m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of the Bhāratavarṣa 6. 10. 37, 5; (तीरग्राहास् तरतोया … ) 6. 10. 51.
तुखार: Tukhāra, Tuṣāra m. (pl.): Name of a people; name Tuṣāra occurs at 6. 71. 20; 12. 65. 13. A. Location: Mentioned by Saṃjaya along with the northern मेल्च्छस् of the Bhāratavarṣa (उत्ताराश् चापरे म्लेच्छा जना … ) 6. 10. 63, 5; (खशीकाश् च तुखा-राश् च) 6. 10. 66; Pāṇḍavas on their return journey from Badarī crossed the country of Tukhāras before reaching Subāhu's realm 3. 174. 12. B. Descrip-tion: Fierce and doing cruel deeds (उग्राश् च क्रूरकर्माणः) 8. 51. 18; wrathful, fond of battles, strong and of firm fists (?) (संरम्भिणो युद्धशौण्डा बलिनो दृब्धपाणयः) 8. 51. 19; nobody except Arjuna could defeat them 8. 51. 20. C. Characteristic: Tuṣāras lived in countries but behaved like दस्युस्; Māndhātṛ asked Indra how they could be made to follow धर्म and how they were to be controll-ed by kings like him 12. 65. 13, 15-16 (for citation see Kahva); Indra then told him their धर्म 12. 65. 17-22; their country was rich in gold and famous for horses (see below Epic events D. No. 1). D. Epic events: (1) They brought to Yudhiṣṭhira as tribute one अर्बुद horses of noble breed and going long distances (महा-गमान् दूरगमान् गणितान् अर्बुदं हयान्) and gold by crores amounting to one पद्म (कोटिशश् चैव बहुशः सुवर्णं पद्मसंमितम्) 2. 47. 26-27; (2) Their kings, afraid of the lustre of weapons (शस्त्रतेजोभयार्दितान्), acted as servers at the Rājasūya sacrifice 3. 48. 18; 21-22; (3) Tukhāras had allied themselves with Duryodhana (एते सुयोधनस्यार्थे सं-रब्धाः कुरुभिः सह) 8. 51. 20; (4) On the sixth day of war, Tuṣāras stood at the right wing of the Krauñcavyūha of the Kauravas 6. 71. 14, 20; (5) On the seventeenth day of war, Tukhāras and others, riding horses, attacked Arjuna; Arjuna cut off with क्षुर arrows their heads and hands holding excellent weapons (तुखारा … सादिनः … वरायुधान् पाणि-गतान् करैः सह … शिरांसि च) 8. 64. 16-17.
तुण्डिकेर: Tuṇḍikera m. (pl.): Name of a people. At the end of the eleventh day of war, Tuṇḍikeras and Mālavas, along with Sudhanvan, took oath to kill Arjuna 7. 16. 18-19; they are mentioned by Saṃjaya among those who were killed during the first seventeen days of war 8. 4. 47.
तुम्बुप: Tumbupa m. (pl.): Name of a people. On the second day of the war, they along with others and led by Nakula and Sahadeva, stood on the left side of the Krauñcāruṇavyūha (Krauñca 6. 47. 1) of the Pāṇḍavas (6. 46. 39, 51).
त्रिगर्त: Trigarta m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada and its people; people occasionally referred to also as Traigarta (7. 17. 6-7, 25) or Traigartaka (7. 17. 5; 7. 136. 3; 14. 73. 27, 31). A. Location: To the north of Indra-prastha: Trigartas mentioned among those Kṣatriyas who gathered together to oppose Arjuna in his expedition to the north before the Rājasūya (प्रययाव् उत्तरां तस्मात् दिशम्) 2. 24. 1; (ततस् त्रिगर्तान् कौन्तेयो  … क्षत्रिया बहवो राजन्न् उपावर्तन्त सर्वशः) 2. 24. 17; the horse of the Aśvamedha went to the north where Arjuna had to fight with the Trigartas (स हयः … ससारोत्तरतः) 14. 72. 21; (त्रिगर्तैर् अभवद् युद्धम् … किरीटिनः) 14. 73. 1; mentioned also among those whom Nakula conquered in his expedition to the west (प्रतीचीं नकुलो … दिशम् व्यजयत्) 2. 23. 10; (निर्याय खाण्डव-प्रस्थात् प्रातीचीम् अभितो दिशम्) 2. 29. 2; (वशे चक्रे … त्रिगर्तान्) 2. 29. 6; but they are listed by Saṃjaya among the Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of the south (अथापरे जनपदा दक्षिणा) 6. 10. 56; त्रिगर्ताः सर्वसेनयः) 6. 10. 59; called Janapada also in 6. 18. 14; 6. 114. 77. B. Description: Brave (शूर) 4. 31. 10; 4. 32. 25; 6. 18. 14; 6. 20. 15; 9. 13. 1; heroic (वीर) 7. 16. 23; very strong (महाबल) 4. 31. 2; (अतिबल) 8. 5. 18; difficult to be defeated (दुर्जय) 8. 5. 18; high-souled (महात्मन्) 6. 78. 13; skilled in archery (कृतास्त्र) 6. 20. 15; arrogant in battles (युद्धदुर्मद) 4. 31. 2; doing cruel acts (क्रूरकारिन्) 7. 99. 5; holding iron clubs in hands (परिघबाहु) 4. 31. 10; proficient in warfare (युद्धविशारद) 7. 99. 5; high-ranking chariot-fighters (महारथ) 4. 24. 8; 9. 13. 1; 11. 26. 36; 14. 73. 31; (महारथसमाज्ञात) 14. 73. 1; (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 14. 74. 1: महारथत्वेन सम्यग् आज्ञातैः); exce-llent chariot-fighters (रथोदार) 5. 163. 9; leaders of Kṣatriyas (क्षत्रियाणाम् धुरंधराः) 5. 163. 13; great archers (महेष्वास) 8. 7. 18; their standards made of gold (सुवर्णविकृतध्वज) 7. 91. 14; 7. 116. 2; their arrows decked with gold (शरा … कार्तस्वरवि-भूषिताः) 9. 13. 5; readiness to die in battle considered as doing one's duty (कृत-कृत्यास् तनुत्यजः) 7. 16. 24; (तनुत्यजः) 6. 18. 14; C. Epic events: (1) After killing Hiḍimba, Pāṇḍavas and Kuntī crossed Matsya, Trigarta, Pāñcāla and Kīcaka countries before they reached Ekacakrā 1. 144. 2; (2) Arjuna conquer-ed Trigartas in his expedition to the north 2. 24. 1 (व्यजयत् … त्रिगर्तान्) 2. 24. 16-17; (3) Mentioned among those who were brought under control by Nakula in his expedition to the west 2. 29. 2, 6; (4) The princely Trigartas (राजन्याः) brought tribute in hundreds for the राजसूय of Yudhiṣṭhira 2. 48. 13, 16; (5) The spies of Duryodhana saw the Trigarta brothers, who were formerly defeated by Kīcaka, seated with Duryo-dhana in his Sabhā 4. 24. 8, 19; (6) Suśar-man suggested to Duryodhana a joint ex-pedition by Kauravas and Trigartas against Matsyas to capture their cattle; Duryodhana suggested that Suśarman, with Trigartas, should first attack the country of Matsyas 4. 29. 11, 23; the cowherds (गोपाः) reported to Virāṭa the capture of cows by hundreds and thousands by Trigartas 4. 30. 7; (7) Matsyas attacked Trigartas at sunset; Matsyas and Trigartas, both long-ing for the cows, fought with one another; they battled with swords, परिघस्, lances, शक्तिस् and तोमरस्; Śatānīka and Viśālā-kṣa entered the large army of the chariot-fighters of Trigartas; Virāṭa attacked Suśarman of Trigartas 4. 31. 1-2, 9, 15-16, 18; when Virāṭa was captured, Matsyas, afflicted by Trigartas, fled in fear; Bhīma, Nakula and Sahadeva marched against Trigartas; they broke the army of Trigartas; Yudhiṣṭhira killed a thousand Trigartas, Bhīma and Nakula seven hundred each, and Sahadeva three hundred warriors of Trigartas; Suśarman, the king of Trigartas, was captured by Bhīma; then, the army of Trigartas was scattered (अभज्यत बलं सर्वं त्रैगर्तम्) 4. 32. 10, 22, 24-25, 32-33; (8) Uttara complained to Arjuna that his father had taken the entire army with him to fight with the Trigartas 4. 36. 15; (9) Duryodhana reminded Bhīṣma that they had gone out to fight with Matsyas for the sake of Trigartas (त्रिगर्-तानां … हेतोः) 4. 42. 9; (10) Virāṭa, after defeating Trigartas, entered his town; he knew that Kurus, after the defeat of Trigartas, would not sit idle; he there-fore ordered the warriors, who were not wounded by Trigartas, to go to help Uttara (ये त्रिगर्तैर् अविक्षताः) 4. 63. 2. 10-11; (11) Principal Trigarta warriors were among those who sided with Duryodhana to fight against Pāṇḍavas (त्रिगर्ताश् च मुख्याः) 5. 30. 23; (12) The five Kekaya brothers on the side of the Pāṇḍavas were to fight, among others, with two chief Trigarta brothers who were among the Saṃśaptakas (त्रिगर्तानां च द्वौ मुख्यौ यौ तौ संशप्तकाव् इति) 5. 56. 18; the sons of Draupadī were to fight with the five Trigarta (brothers) 5. 161. 8; (13) Before the start of war, Trigartas mentioned among the twelve Janapadas who with their large armies of chariot-fighters (महता रथवंशेन) were to protect Bhīṣma 6. 18. 13-14; (14) On the first day of war, brave Trigartas were ready to take on Arjuna (येनार्जुनस् तेन … प्रयाता … ) 6. 20. 15; (15) On the second day, Duryodhana wanted to protect Bhīṣma with the help of Trigartas and others 6. 47. 7; (16) On the third day, Trigar-tas stood at the head of the Garuḍavyūha of the Kauravas 6. 52. 2, 4; (17) On the fourth day, Trigartas were among those who attacked Arjuna and Abhi-manyu 6. 57. 12; (18) On the fifth day, when Arjuna attacked Bhīṣma, Trigartas and others, afraid, took shelter with the king of Kaliṅga 6. 67. 13; the same day Nakula fought with the high-ranking chariot-fighters of Trigartas (त्रिगर्तानां रथोदारैः) 6. 68. 7; (19) On the seventh day, Bhīṣma was surrounded on all sides by Trigartas when he marched ahead to attack Arjuna 6. 78. 13; (20) On the ninth day, Duryodhana, with Trigartas standing on all sides, took position in the middle of the Sarvatobhadravyūha 6. 95. 31, 26; even though Trigartas were getting killed by Arjuna they, risking their life, attacked Arjuna and showered him with arrows; Arjuna then released Vāyavyāstra on them 6. 98. 14-15, 18; (21) On the tenth day, Bhīma and Arjuna harassed the large army of Trigartas (अपीडयेतां समरे त्रिगर्तानां महद् बलम्) 6. 110. 8; incited by Duryodhana (6. 112. 102-107), Trigartas attacked Arjuna as do moths the flame of fire (पतङ्गा इव पाव-कम्) 6. 112. 110; Trigartas were among the twelve Janapadas who did not abandon Bhīṣma although they were pierced by arrows and afflicted by wounds (शरार्ता व्रणपी दिताः) 6. 114. 77; (22) On the ele-venth day, Karṇa led Trigartas and other warriors who formed the Śakaṭavyūha 7. 6. 6, 15; (23) Kṛṣṇa's defeating the Trigartas mentioned by Dhṛtarāṣṭra to Saṃjaya 7. 10. 17; (24) On the twelfth day, Satyaratha vowed that by the end of that day the earth would be either with-out Arjuna or without the Trigartas (specifically the five Trigarta brothers: Satyaratha, Satyadharman, Satyavarman, Satyeṣu and Satyakarman) (अद्यास्त्व् अनर्-जुना भूमिर् अत्रिगर्ताथ वा पुनः) 7. 16. 16-18; that day, Arjuna left to fight with Trigartas 7. 16. 47; Suśarman with his five brothers and an अयुत chariot-fighters took an oath in the presence of fire to kill Arjuna; the mode of taking oath descri-bed 7. 16. 19-36; Arjuna was first surprised to see Traigartaka brothers delighted when they should have wept, but then felt that Traigartas were delighted because they would attain best worlds (after death); he then assailed the army of Traigartas which was ready in a formation (भ्रा-तॄंस् त्रैगर्तकान् … अथ वा हर्षकालो ऽयं त्रैगर्तानाम् असंशयम् … आससाद रणे व्यूढां त्रैगर्तानाम् अनीकिनीम्) 7. 17. 5-7; Traigartas afraid when Sudhanvan was killed by Arjuna (त्रैगर्तान् भयम् आविशत्) 7. 17. 25; they were confused when they were being killed by Arjuna; Suśar-man exhorted them to take courage and fight in accordance with the oath taken by them; they then returned to fight till death 7. 17. 26-31; Arjuna harassed Trigr-tas and others with his arrows and killed them; they in return showered arrows so that neither he, his chariot, not Kṛṣṇa could be seen; Trigartas, feeling that Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna were killed, shook with delight their upper garments (वासांस्य् आदुधुवुस् तदा) and blew by thousands भेरिस्, मृदङ्गस् and conches 7. 18. 16-20; of the fourteen thousand Saṃśaptaka warriors (who had taken oath) who attacked Arjuna, ten thousand were Tri-gartas (and four thousand Gopālas) 7. 26. 10-11; (25) On the fourteenth day, Duryodhana, accompanied by a striking force of a thousand chariot-fighters of Trigartas, went to attack Arjuna (रथा-नां च सहस्रेण त्रिगर्तानां प्रहारिणां) 7. 69. 72; when Niramitra (son of Suśar-man) was killed a great roar of grief went up from the Trigartas 7. 82. 27-29; Sātyaki saw that the excellent Trigarta chariot-fighters (त्रिगरतानां रथोदाराः) stood in readiness to fight with him; so he asked his charioteer to drive his chariot to them so that he could engage them in a battle in the presence of Droṇa (त्रिगर्तैः सह योत्स्यामि भारद्वाजस्य पश्यतः) 7. 91. 14-15; when Duḥśāsana was covered with arrows, Duryodhana asked Trigartas to attack Sātyaki; three thousand Trigar-tas, skilled in warfare, then surrounded Sātyaki; Sātyaki killed five hundred of them; afraid, they took shelter with Droṇa 7. 99. 4-13; when Duḥśāsana lost his chariot, the general of the Trigarta army took him away in his chariot 7. 99. 25; a host of Trigarta archers, fight-ing from chariots, surrounded Sātyaki; Sātyaki, alone, defeated fifty (Trigarta) princes; Trigartas, afflicted, returned to their own people (त्रिगर्ताः संन्यवर्-तन्त संतप्ताः स्वजनं प्रति) 7. 116. 2; (26) During the night war, Yudhiṣṭhira killed a number of Trigartas 7. 132. 23; (त्रैगर्तकान्) 7. 136. 3; Duryodhana asked the surviving great warriors among Trigartas to stay in front of Droṇa (त्रि-गर्तानां च ये शूरा हतशिष्टा महा-रथाः) 7. 139. 19; (27) Dhṛtarāṣṭra remembered that Karṇa had formerly defeated Trigartas 8. 5. 18; (28) On the sixteenth day, Kṛpa, along with Trigartas, stood at the place of the right foot of the Makaravyūha of the Kauravas 8. 7. 18, 14; Trigartas and others, along with Kauravas marched against Arjuna; they did not abandon fighting with Arjuna though they got killed by him (ते वध्यमानाः समरे नाजहुः पाण्डवं तदा) 8. 19. 2, 7; in the afternoon of that day (अपराह्णे) Arjuna killed Trigartas 8. 19. 74-75; (29) On the seventeenth day, when Ulūka lost his horse and charioteer, he jumped down from his chariot and took shelter with the large army of Trigartas (त्रिगर्तानां बलं पूर्णं जगाम) 8. 44. 41; (30) On the eighteenth day, Kṛtavarman, with Trigartas all around him, stood on the left side of the Sarvatobhadravyūha of the Kauravas 9. 7. 24, 19; Arjuna was pierced with many arrows by Aśvatthāman and by the great Trigarta chariot-fighters (त्रिगतानां महा-रथैः); they did not leave fighting with Arjuna though they were getting killed with sharp arrows 9. 13. 1, 3; Arjuna attacked Trigartas and killed their horses and broke their chariots; then the great chariot-fighters of Trigartas gathered to-gether and showered arrows on Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna 9. 26. 34-35; (31) Vidura and others cremated the dead bodies of the great Trigarta chariot-fighters (त्रिगर्तांश् च महारथान्) 11. 26. 36; (32) Arjuna, while following the Aśvamedha horse, had to fight with the sons and grand-sons of Trigartas, famous as महारथस्, with whom he had formed enmity during the great war; at one stage the Traigartaka warriors encircled Arjuna; (the battle des-cribed in 14. 73. 3-33) (जिष्नुं त्रैगर्तका योधास् त्वरिताः पर्यवारयन्) 14. 73. 1, 27; afflicted by Arjuna's arrows, dejected, they fled in all directions (त्रैगर्तक-महारथाः । दिशो विदुद्रुवुः सर्वा … ) 14. 73. 31; ultimately they all surrendered (तव स्म किंकराः सर्वे सर्वे च वशगास् तव) 14. 73. 32-33. D. Various persons, especially Suśarman (who is not always directly mentioned), referred to as the king of Trigartas or chief warrior of Tri-gartas, or simply as belonging to Trigartas; त्रिगर्तराज्: Suśarman 7. 17. 27; 6. 81. 10; 6. 98. 10; त्रिगर्तराज: (1) Kṣemaṃkara 3. 249. 6; (2) Suratha 3. 255. 18; (3) Suśarman 3. 249. 6; 3. 255. 18; 4. 32. 32; 6. 77. 3, 34; 6. 81. 4, 8; 6. 98. 13; 6. 104. 57; 7. 82. 27; 8. 19. 4; त्रिगर्तराजन्: Suśar-man (त्रिगर्तानां राजा) 4. 29. 1; Sūrya-varman 14. 73. 9; त्रिगर्ताधिपति: (1) Satyaratha 7. 16. 11 (17); (2) Suśarman 4. 32. 7; 6. 100. 10; 7. 27. 6, 8; 9. 2. 18; 9. 26. 16; त्रिगर्तानां महारथः: (1) Vīradhanvan 7. 82. 18; (2) Suśar-man 4. 32. 33; त्रिगर्त: Suśarman 6. 83. 10, 11; 6. 109. 47; 7. 16. 19; 9. 2. 34 (त्रिगर्तश् च जनाधिपः); त्रैगर्त: Suśarman 4. 32. 4, 30; 6. 100. 8; त्रैगर्ती (f.) Yaśodharā, princess of Trigarta 1. 90. 37 [See Prasthala, Saṃśaptaka].
त्रैपुर: Traipura m. (pl.): Designation of the warriors of Tripura. On the eighth day of war, Traipuras accompanied Bṛhadbala, king of Kosala, who stood behind Bhagadatta in the Mahāvyūha (6. 83. 5) of the Kauravas (कौसल्यो थ बृहद्बलः । त्रैपुरैश् चैव … समन्वितः) 6. 83. 9.
त्र्यक्ष: Tryakṣa m. (pl.): Name of a people (having three eyes ?). Mentioned among those who brought tribute in the form of gold and silver in large quantities for the Rājasūya, but were stopped at the gate (बल्यर्थं ददतस् तस्मै हिरण्यं रजतं बहु) 2. 47. 15-16 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 2. 51. 17: द्व्यक्षादयः प्राच्यदेशभेदाः).
त्र्यङ्ग: Tryaṅga m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada. Mentioned by Saṃjaya among the southern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of the Bhāratavarṣa (अथापरे जनपदा दक्षिणा … 6. 10. 56, 5); (त्र्यङ्गाः केकरकाः प्रोष्ठाः) 6. 10. 60.
